ko_meaning: 다리 끝에 있고 걸을 때 땅에 닿는 몸의 부분
ko_meaning_en: The part of the body at the end of the leg that touches the ground when you walk

example.en: The baby's feet are small.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject (after a consonant)

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'feet' the subject.
form.why: 발 ends in a consonant (ㄹ), so the subject marker is 이. 가 follows a vowel, 을 marks an object, and 에 means 'at/to'.

ko_meaning: 목 위에 있는 몸의 부분, 또는 거기에 나는 털
ko_meaning_en: The part of the body above the neck, or the hair that grows there

example.en: My older sister has long hair.

tokens.note: 는 marks the topic (after a vowel)
가 marks the subject (after a vowel)

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 길다 (to be long).
form.why: The last vowel of 길다 is ㅣ (not ㅏ or ㅗ), so it takes -어요: 길어요.

ko_meaning: 눈, 코, 입이 있는 머리의 앞쪽
ko_meaning_en: The front of the head, where the eyes, nose and mouth are

example.en: The child washes their face.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject (after a vowel)
을 marks the object (after a consonant)

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'face' the object.
form.why: 얼굴 ends in a consonant, so the object marker is 을. 를 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning: 몸 아래에 있고 서거나 걸을 때 쓰는 긴 부분
ko_meaning_en: The long part at the bottom of the body that you use to stand or walk

example.en: My legs hurt yesterday.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject (after a vowel)
past tense, polite; 아프다 drops ㅡ (아프 + 았어요)

form.q_en: Pick the correct form for 'hurt (yesterday)'.
form.why: 어제 needs the past tense. 아프다 drops ㅡ and takes -았어요: 아팠어요.

ko_meaning: 가슴 아래에 있는 몸의 앞부분, 음식이 들어가는 곳
ko_meaning_en: The front of the body below the chest, where food goes

example.en: Grandpa has a big belly.

tokens.note: 는 marks the topic (after a vowel)
가 marks the subject (after a vowel)
present tense, polite; 크다 drops ㅡ (크 + 어요)

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 크다 (to be big).
form.why: 크다 drops ㅡ before -어요, so it becomes 커요.

ko_meaning: 수를 셀 때 맨 처음 수, 1
ko_meaning_en: The very first number when counting, 1

example.en: One apple, please.

tokens.note: native number, used alone without a counter

form.q_en: Pick the number for 'one apple' (no counter word).
form.why: Counting things without a counter uses the native number 하나. 한 is only used right before a counter, and 일 is Sino-Korean.

ko_meaning_en: One plus one, 2

example.en: I have two younger siblings.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject (after a consonant)
native number, used alone without a counter

form.q_en: Pick the right form of 'two' before the counter 명 (people).
form.why: Before a counter, 둘 becomes 두: 두 명. 이 is Sino-Korean and is not used to count people.

ko_meaning_en: Two plus one, 3

example.en: There are three of us in my family.

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic (after a consonant)

form.q_en: Pick the right ending for 'is three'.
form.why: 셋 ends in a consonant, so it takes 이에요. 예요 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: Three plus one, 4

example.en: A dog has four legs.

tokens.note: 는 marks the topic (after a vowel)
가 marks the subject (after a vowel)

form.q_en: Pick the number for 'four legs' (no counter word).
form.why: Counting things uses the native number 넷. 네 is only used right before a counter, and 사 is Sino-Korean.

ko_meaning_en: Four plus one, 5

example.en: I bought five pieces of bread.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object (after a consonant)

form.q_en: Pick the number for 'five' with the counter 개 (things).
form.why: The counter 개 uses native numbers: 다섯 개. 오 and 일 are Sino-Korean.

ko_meaning_en: Five plus one, 6

example.en: The child is six years old.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject (after a vowel)

form.q_en: Pick the number for age with 살 (years old).
form.why: Age with 살 uses native numbers: 여섯 살. 육 is Sino-Korean.

ko_meaning_en: Six plus one, 7

example.en: I get up at seven in the morning.

form.q_en: Pick the number for 'seven o'clock'.
form.why: Hours (시) use native numbers: 일곱 시. Minutes (분) use Sino-Korean numbers.

ko_meaning_en: Seven plus one, 8

example.en: There are eight students.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject (after a consonant)
native number; spelled ㄼ but said 여덜

form.q_en: Pick the correct number for 'eight people'.
form.why: People (명) are counted with native numbers: 여덟 명. It is spelled 여덟 (ㄼ), even though it sounds like 여덜.

ko_meaning_en: Eight plus one, 9

example.en: My older brother ate nine apples.

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic (after a consonant)
를 marks the object (after a vowel)

form.q_en: Pick the number for 'nine' with the counter 개.
form.why: The counter 개 uses native numbers: 아홉 개. 구 is Sino-Korean.

ko_meaning_en: Nine plus one, 10

example.en: Dad worked for ten hours.

tokens.note: 는 marks the topic (after a vowel)

form.q_en: Pick the number for 'ten hours'.
form.why: 시간 (hours of time) uses native numbers: 열 시간. 십 is Sino-Korean.

ko_meaning: 날짜, 돈, 층을 말할 때 쓰는 수 1
ko_meaning_en: The number 1 used for dates, money and floors

example.en: There is a bank on the first floor.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject (after a consonant)

form.q_en: Pick the number for 'first floor'.
form.why: Floors (층) use Sino-Korean numbers: 일 층. Native 하나 is not used with 층.

ko_meaning: 날짜, 돈, 학년을 말할 때 쓰는 수 2
ko_meaning_en: The number 2 used for dates, money and school years

example.en: My younger sibling is in second grade.

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic (after a consonant)

form.q_en: Pick the number for 'second grade'.
form.why: School years (학년) use Sino-Korean numbers: 이 학년. 둘 and 두 are native.

ko_meaning: 날짜, 돈, 분을 말할 때 쓰는 수 3
ko_meaning_en: The number 3 used for dates, money and minutes

example.en: I waited three minutes for the bus.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object (after a vowel)

form.q_en: Pick the number for 'three minutes'.
form.why: Minutes (분) use Sino-Korean numbers: 삼 분. 셋 is native.

ko_meaning: 날짜, 달, 돈을 말할 때 쓰는 수 4
ko_meaning_en: The number 4 used for dates, months and money

example.en: I'm going to Korea in April.

tokens.note: 사월 = 사 (4) + 월 (month); 에 = 'in' a time

form.q_en: Pick the number for 'April' (month 4).
form.why: Months use Sino-Korean numbers: 사월 (April). Native 넷/네 are never used for months.

ko_meaning: 돈, 날짜, 번호를 말할 때 쓰는 수 5
ko_meaning_en: The number 5 used for money, dates and numbers

example.en: The milk is 500 won.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject (after a vowel)

form.q_en: Pick the number for '500 won'.
form.why: Prices use Sino-Korean numbers: 오백 원. 다섯 is native.

ko_meaning: 날짜, 돈, 번호를 말할 때 쓰는 수 6
ko_meaning_en: The number 6 used for dates, money and numbers

example.en: My younger sibling's birthday is on the sixth.

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic (after a consonant)
일 here = day of the month

form.q_en: Pick the number for 'the sixth' (a date).
form.why: Dates use Sino-Korean numbers: 육 일 (the 6th). Native 여섯 is not used for dates.

ko_meaning: 날짜, 달, 돈을 말할 때 쓰는 수 7
ko_meaning_en: The number 7 used for dates, months and money

example.en: July is very hot.

tokens.note: 칠월 = 칠 (7) + 월 (month); 은 marks the topic

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 덥다 (to be hot).
form.why: 덥다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ changes to 우 before -어요, so it becomes 더워요.

ko_meaning: 날짜, 달, 돈을 말할 때 쓰는 수 8
ko_meaning_en: The number 8 used for dates, months and money

example.en: I want to go to the sea in August.

tokens.note: 팔월 = 팔 (8) + 월 (month); 에 = 'in' a time

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'in August'.
form.why: Time words such as months take 에: 팔월에 (in August). 에서 is for the place where an action happens.

ko_meaning: 번호, 날짜, 돈을 말할 때 쓰는 수 9
ko_meaning_en: The number 9 used for numbers, dates and money

example.en: I take bus number 9.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object (after a vowel)

form.q_en: Pick the particle that goes with 타다 (to ride).
form.why: 타다 takes an object marker: 버스를 타요. 버스 ends in a vowel, so use 를, not 을.

ko_meaning: 분, 날짜, 돈을 말할 때 쓰는 수 10
ko_meaning_en: The number 10 used for minutes, dates and money

example.en: I walk for ten minutes every day.

tokens.note: 분 = minute; minutes use Sino-Korean numbers

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 걷다 (to walk).
form.why: 걷다 is ㄷ-irregular: ㄷ becomes ㄹ before a vowel, so it becomes 걸어요.

ko_meaning_en: Ten times ten, 100

example.en: There are a hundred people in the park.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject (after a consonant)

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the place with 있다 (there is).
form.why: 있다 (there is) uses 에 for the place: 공원에 있어요. 에서 is for places where an action happens.

ko_meaning_en: Ten times a hundred, 1,000

example.en: Mom gave me 1,000 won.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject (after a vowel)
1,000 is just 천 (no 일 before it)
을 marks the object (after a consonant)

form.q_en: Pick the correct past form of 주다 (to give).
form.why: 주다 + -었어요 shortens to 줬어요.

ko_meaning_en: Ten times a thousand, 10,000

example.en: I bought the gift for 10,000 won.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object (after a consonant)
Korean counts big numbers in units of 만 (10,000)

form.q_en: Pick the Korean word for 10,000.
form.why: Korean has its own unit for 10,000: 만. It is never 십천 or 열천 ('ten thousand').

ko_meaning_en: The unit of Korean money

example.en: Korean money is the won.

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic (after a consonant)

form.q_en: Pick the right ending for 'is the won'.
form.why: 원 ends in a consonant, so it takes 이에요. 예요 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: What you pay with when you buy things

example.en: I don't have any money now.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject (after a consonant)

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'money' with 없다 (to not have).
form.why: With 있다/없다, the thing you have or lack takes 이/가. 돈 ends in a consonant, so use 이.

ko_meaning_en: This day, the day it is now

example.en: The weather is nice today.

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic (after a consonant)
가 marks the subject (after a vowel)

form.q_en: Pick the topic particle for 'today'.
form.why: 오늘 ends in a consonant (ㄹ), so the topic marker is 은. 는 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: The day before today

example.en: I met a friend yesterday.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object (after a vowel)

form.q_en: Pick the verb form that fits 'yesterday'.
form.why: 어제 (yesterday) needs the past tense: 만나다 → 만났어요.

ko_meaning_en: The day after today

example.en: I'm going to school tomorrow.

tokens.note: the present tense can talk about the near future

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where you go.
form.why: With 가다 (to go), the destination takes 에: 학교에 가요.

ko_meaning_en: This very moment

example.en: It's raining now.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject (after a vowel)
오 + 아요 → 와요; in Korean, rain 'comes'

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 오다 (to come).
form.why: 오다 + -아요 shortens to 와요. Korean says rain 'comes': 비가 와요.

ko_meaning: 어떤 때부터 어떤 때까지의 동안, 또는 60분
ko_meaning_en: The length between two moments, or 60 minutes

example.en: Do you have time today?

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject (after a consonant)
rising intonation makes it a question

form.q_en: Pick the right form of 'two' before 시간 (hours).
form.why: 시간 (hours) uses native numbers, and 둘 becomes 두 before it: 두 시간.

ko_meaning: 해가 뜨고 하루가 시작되는 때, 또는 그때 먹는 밥
ko_meaning_en: The time when the sun rises and the day begins, or the meal eaten then

example.en: Did you eat breakfast today?

tokens.note: 을 marks the object (after a consonant)
past tense, polite (-었어요); rising intonation = question

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'breakfast' the object.
form.why: 아침 ends in a consonant, so the object marker is 을. 를 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning: 하루의 가운데 때, 또는 그때 먹는 밥
ko_meaning_en: The middle of the day, or the meal eaten then

example.en: I go to a restaurant at lunchtime.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where you go.
form.why: With 가다 (to go), the place you go to takes 에: 식당에 가요.

ko_meaning: 해가 지고 밤이 되기 전의 때, 또는 그때 먹는 밥
ko_meaning_en: The time after sunset before night, or the meal eaten then

example.en: I want to have dinner with my family.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object (after a consonant)

form.q_en: Pick the particle that means 'with'.
form.why: 하고 means 'with' (or 'and'): 가족하고 = with my family.

ko_meaning_en: The dark time after the sun sets

example.en: The stars are pretty at night.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject (after a consonant)
예쁘다 drops ㅡ: 예쁘 + 어요 → 예뻐요

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 예쁘다 (to be pretty).
form.why: 예쁘다 drops ㅡ before -어요, so it becomes 예뻐요.

ko_meaning_en: The bright time when the sun is up

example.en: The child plays in the park during the day.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject (after a vowel)
에서 = place where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the right form for 'during the day'.
form.why: Time words take 에: 낮에 (during the day). 에서 is for places, not times.

ko_meaning_en: The day after Sunday

example.en: I go to the office on Monday.

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 가다 (to go).
form.why: 가다 + -아요 shortens to 가요 (the two ㅏ sounds merge).

ko_meaning_en: The day after Monday

example.en: Today is Tuesday.

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic (after a consonant)

form.q_en: Pick the right ending for 'is Tuesday'.
form.why: 화요일 ends in a consonant (ㄹ), so it takes 이에요. 예요 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: The day after Tuesday

example.en: I have an exam on Wednesday.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject (after a consonant)

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'on Wednesday'.
form.why: Days of the week take 에 for 'on': 수요일에 (on Wednesday).

ko_meaning_en: The day after Wednesday

example.en: I study at the library on Thursday.

tokens.note: 에서 = place where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 공부하다 (to study).
form.why: 하다 verbs end in 해요 in the polite present: 공부하다 → 공부해요.

ko_meaning_en: The day after Thursday

example.en: I watch a movie on Friday night.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object (after a vowel)

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'movie' the object.
form.why: 영화 ends in a vowel, so the object marker is 를. 을 follows a consonant.

ko_meaning_en: The day after Friday

example.en: I want to go to the mountains on Saturday.

form.q_en: Pick the right form for 'want to go'.
form.why: 'Want to' is the verb stem + -고 싶어요: 가고 싶어요.

ko_meaning_en: The day after Saturday

example.en: I rest at home on Sunday.

tokens.note: 에서 = place where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the place where you rest.
form.why: 쉬다 (to rest) is an action, so the place takes 에서: 집에서 쉬어요. 에 is for where you go or where something is.

ko_meaning_en: Saturday and Sunday

example.en: I hang out with my friends on the weekend.

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 놀다 (to hang out).
form.why: 놀다 has the vowel ㅗ, so it takes -아요: 놀아요.

ko_meaning_en: Seven days, from Monday to Sunday

example.en: I exercise three times a week.

tokens.note: 셋 becomes 세 before a counter
번 = counter for how many times

form.q_en: Pick the right form of 'three' before 번 (times).
form.why: 번 (times) uses native numbers, and 셋 becomes 세 before a counter: 세 번.

ko_meaning_en: The day you were born

example.en: Tomorrow is Mom's birthday.

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic (after a consonant)
no 의 needed: 엄마 생일 = mom's birthday

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'on the birthday'.
form.why: A day or time takes 에 for 'on': 생일에 (on the birthday). 에서 is for places.
